pages.title: A comparison requires an invariance choice

A comparison requires an invariance choice
Raw coordinate RMS includes pose, cyclic start and shape.
We remove proper rigid
motion and cyclic start while retaining physical scale and traversal direction.

pages.title: Enumerate the starting index
pages.text:
Enumerate the starting index
For each k, center the arrays, solve the proper Procrustes problem, and retain the smallest
residual.
The identity choice guarantees drc ≤ dRMS.

pages.title: Retained geometric differences
pages.text:
Retained geometric diﬀerences
Rigid copies and cyclic reindexings can have zero aligned discrepancy.
Size and local
displacement remain nonzero because neither is removed by the allowed transformations.

pages.title: A quadratic neighbor penalty
pages.text:
A quadratic neighbor penalty
Eλ(u) = 1n ∑j ∥uj∥2 + λn ∑j ∥uj+1 − uj∥2.
Eλ has units mm 2; λ ≥ 0 is dimensionless.
Computational Cardiology Notes 10 / 20

A quadratic neighbor penalty
Eλ(u) = 1n ∑j ∥uj∥2 + λn ∑j ∥uj+1 − uj∥2.

pages.title: Matrix form of the score
pages.text:
Matrix form of the score
Eλ(u) = 1n uT(I + λDTD)u.
The identity term makes the matrix positive deﬁnite.

The grid is part of this deﬁnition

interpretation as a derivative penalty.

pages.title: Nonoriented geometric comparison
pages.text:
Nonoriented geometric comparison
Positions, geometric weights and tangent or normal directions deﬁne an endpoint
representation.
Squared directional dot products can identify opposite orientations. Kernel
scale controls spatial sensitivity.

pages.title: The implemented and contextual calculations
pages.text:
The implemented and contextual calculations
The companion computes ﬁnite cyclic alignment and a quadratic displacement score.
Elastic surface paths and varifold registration remain research context, with additional
geometry, optimization and numerical requirements.
